name: EmailOctopus
tagline: Manage a small subscriber list and send compliant campaigns through a hosted provider

pricing.notes: Typical entry paid tier at low subscriber count.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails/month, 30-day reporting, 1 landing page, 1 form, 1 user, EmailOctopus branding.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Starting tier shown with 10,000 emails/month; unlimited landing pages, forms and users; reports kept forever.
tiers.notes: Annual card showed $9/mo billed yearly; monthly dollar amount not exposed in crawled text.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; 2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails/month, 1 landing page, 1 form, 1 user, 30-day reports, branding.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual card shows $9/mo billed yearly and a yearly saving; monthly price not exposed in crawl
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid price scales by subscriber/send tier; Free plan keeps reports for only 30 days and includes EmailOctopus branding.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For EmailOctopus, manage a small subscriber list and send compliant campaigns through a hosted provider. The hard boundary is deliverability, templates, automations, landing pages, and customer support, plus deliverability, growth network, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Manage a small subscriber list, compose and send compliant campaigns through a hosted provider, publish a web archive, and report basic delivery and click events.
whatYouLose: deliverability, templates, automations, landing pages, and customer support
ongoingBurden: DNS authentication, reputation, bounces, complaints, unsubscribe compliance, templates, queues, analytics, backups, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for EmailOctopus because newsletter operators pay for inbox placement, growth mechanics, and operational confidence on publication day. The recurring cost buys DNS authentication, reputation, bounces, complaints, unsubscribe compliance, templates, queues, analytics, backups, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Listmonk
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: A huge contact allowance with a tiny daily send pipe; suitable when low volume is literal.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, consent records, and message events live in Brevo's cloud; contacts can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo Free stores many contacts and supports campaigns, but a 300-message daily pipe is less flexible than EmailOctopus for sending a modest list in one batch.
facts.setupBlocker: Authenticating a custom sending domain requires adding DNS records.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: The vendor's own free plan covers 2,500 contacts and 10,000 monthly emails; branding and automation limits remain.

facts.dataFormat: Lists, campaigns, automations, and reporting data live in EmailOctopus' cloud; contacts and reports can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: EmailOctopus Free is the same hosted product, but its 2,500-contact, 10,000-email, three-automation, branding, and 30-day-reporting limits remain.
facts.setupBlocker: You must verify a sender address or domain; DNS authentication is the first technical step.

alternatives.name: Keila
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted list, forms and campaigns without contact caps; you supply deliverability.

facts.install: Keila Cloud signup or Docker image plus PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted subscribers, campaigns, and job state live in PostgreSQL; uploaded campaign assets live on persistent server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Keila removes contact pricing, but you must supply the server, SMTP provider, deliverability monitoring, backups, and updates that EmailOctopus manages.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, PostgreSQL, a public HTTPS domain, and credentials for SMTP, SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, or Postmark.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited sends and forms for up to 10,000 subscribers; one built-in recommendation slot belongs to Kit.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, tags, forms, broadcasts, sequences, purchases, and analytics live in Kit's cloud; subscriber and chart data export as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kit Free permits more subscribers and unlimited sends, but its single sequence/automation and Kit-controlled recommendation slot make it less neutral and flexible.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no software install, but custom-domain sending requires DNS authentication and the free plan keeps one Kit-managed recommendation slot.

alternatives.name: listmonk
alternatives.desc: The lean self-hosted answer for lists and campaigns; setup is one compose file plus an SMTP account.

facts.install: Docker Compose or a single release binary plus PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, templates, and analytics live in a PostgreSQL database on your server.
facts.gapVsPaid: listmonk is lean and uncapped by contacts, but it replaces EmailOctopus' managed deliverability and support with your own server, PostgreSQL, and sender.
facts.setupBlocker: You still need a PostgreSQL database and a trustworthy SMTP/API sender with authenticated DNS.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: A larger useful free allowance with campaigns, forms and automations; one user only.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, automations, and engagement events live in Sender's cloud; subscriber data can be exported.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender Free has a useful allowance and more automation, but its one-user free account and vendor branding are worse for collaboration and presentation.
facts.setupBlocker: A custom sending domain must be verified with DNS records for reliable delivery.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a single-publication newsletter DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for EmailOctopus in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Amazon SES; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage a small subscriber list, compose and send compliant campaigns through a hosted provider, publish a web archive, and report basic delivery and click events.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement subscriber import, double opt-in, unsubscribe, suppression, tags, and consent timestamps.
Create a Markdown campaign editor with HTML and plain-text previews.
Queue sends through SES with retries, rate limits, idempotency, and resumable batches.
Process delivery, bounce, complaint, open, and click webhooks without logging message content.
Publish a simple issue archive and subscriber preference page.
Add test sends, seed-list checks, DNS setup guidance, exports, and backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a newsletter recommendation marketplace.
Deliberately leave out ad sales and payment infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out complex lifecycle automation and enterprise deliverability support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
